facts.statement: Guaibasaurus is an extinct basal saurischian dinosaur found in the Late Triassic Caturrita Formation of southern Brazil.
facts.quote: Guaibasaurus is an extinct genus of basal saurischian dinosaur known from the Late Triassic Caturrita Formation of Rio Grande do Sul, southern Brazil.

facts.statement: Estimates for Guaibasaurus size vary, with Gregory S. Paul (2016) suggesting it was about 2 meters long and 10 kg, while Molina-Pérez and Larramendi (2020) estimated it at 3 meters long and 35 kg.
facts.quote: In 2016 Gregory S. Paul estimated it at around 2 meters long (6.6 ft) and 10 kg (22 lbs), whereas in 2020 Molina-Pérez and Larramendi listed it at 3 meters (10 ft) and 35 kg (77 lbs).

facts.statement: Guaibasaurus is described as a small, lightly built dinosaur with a length of about 2 meters.
facts.quote: Guaibasaurus es un pequeño dinosaurio de construcción ligera con una longitud de unos 2 metros.

facts.statement: The femur of specimen UFRGS PV0725T measures 27 centimeters in length.
facts.quote: El fémur de UFRGS PV0725T tiene una longitud de 27 centímetros.

facts.statement: Basic anatomical features include four fingers in the hand, four toes in the foot with the fifth toe reduced to a single metatarsal, an almost closed acetabulum at the hip joint, and a high medial ridge on a narrow calcaneus.
facts.quote: Las características básicas son la posesión de cuatro dedos en la mano, cuatro dedos en el pie, mientras que el quinto dedo se reduce a un solo metatarsiano; un acetábulo casi cerrado en la articulación de la cadera y una arista media alta en un calcáneo estrecho.

facts.statement: Guaibasaurus was first named by José F. Bonaparte, Jorge Ferigolo, and Ana Maria Ribeiro in 1999, with the type species being Guaibasaurus candelariensis.
facts.quote: Guaibasaurus was first named by José F. Bonaparte, Jorge Ferigolo and Ana Maria Ribeiro in 1999 and the type species is Guaibasaurus candelariensis.

facts.statement: Specimens date to the early Norian faunal stage of the Late Triassic, found in the lower Caturrita Formation or uppermost Santa Maria 2 Sequence.
facts.quote: All specimen were collected in these two localities from the lower portion of the Caturrita Formation (Rosário do Sul Group, Paraná Basin) or alternatively the uppermost Santa Maria 2 Sequence, dating to the early Norian faunal stage of the Late Triassic.

facts.statement: Guaibasaurus lived during the Late Triassic, approximately 227.4 to 220.7 million years ago, in what is now South America.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Triásico, hace aproximadamente 227,4 y 220,7 millones de años, durante el Carniense, en lo que hoy es Sudamérica.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Guaibasaurus may have rested in a bird-like posture to conserve body heat.
facts.quote: Like living birds, Guaibasaurus may have rested in this position to conserve body heat.

facts.statement: Most analyses classify Guaibasaurus as a sauropodomorph, though some studies suggest it was a theropod.
facts.quote: Most analyses recover it as a sauropodomorph, although there are some suggestions that it was a theropod instead.

facts.statement: Recent cladistic analyses disagree on Guaibasaurus classification, with some finding it a basal theropod and others a basal sauropodomorph.
facts.quote: More recent cladistic analyses have disagreed on the placement of Guaibasaurus. Some analyses have found it to be a basal theropod, while others consider it a basal sauropodomorph.

facts.statement: It is debated whether other members of Guaibasauridae, such as Saturnalia, form a clade with Guaibasaurus, as they are generally considered very basal sauropodomorphs.
facts.quote: Other members of "Guaibasauridae" (such as Saturnalia) are generally considered to be very basal sauropodomorphs, and may or may not form a clade with Guaibasaurus.

facts.statement: Guaibasaurus is classified in the family Guaibasauridae.
facts.quote: familia: Guaibasauridae

facts.statement: The genus authority for Guaibasaurus is Bonaparte et al., 1999.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Bonaparte et al., 1999

facts.statement: The species authority for Guaibasaurus candelariensis is Bonaparte et al., 1999.
facts.quote: species_authority: Bonaparte et al., 1999

facts.statement: The genus Guaibasaurus was described by José Bonaparte and colleagues in 1999.
facts.quote: José Bonaparte y sus colegas, en su descripción de 1999 del género

facts.statement: Bonaparte and colleagues placed the genus in its own family, Guaibasauridae.
facts.quote: lo colocaron en su propia familia , Guaibasauridae

facts.statement: In 2007, Bonaparte and colleagues placed the similar Brazilian dinosaur Saturnalia in the same family, Guaibasauridae.
facts.quote: Bonaparte y sus colegas en 2007 encontraron a Saturnalia un nuevo dinosaurio brasileño muy similar a este, y colocaron a los dos en Guaibasauridae

facts.statement: Bonaparte suggested that these forms might be primitive sauropodomorphs or a group of forms near the common ancestor of sauropodomorphs and theropods.
facts.quote: Bonaparte descubrió que estas formas pueden haber sido sauropodomorfos primitivos, o un conjunto de formas cercanas al ancestro común de los sauropodomorfos y terópodos

facts.statement: The parent group of the genus Guaibasaurus is Guaibasauridae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Guaibasauridae

facts.statement: Guaibasaurus is classified in the class Saurischia.
facts.quote: Class: Saurischia

facts.statement: Guaibasaurus lived during the Norian stage, from 227.3 to 205.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Norian to Norian (227.3 to 205.7 million years ago)

facts.statement: There are three recorded fossil occurrences of Guaibasaurus in the Paleobiology Database.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 3
